title: Best way to use ChatGPT for gamedev
author: Rhytmik
selftext:
Hello,   
I'm currently learning to use AI to build my own game and so far using chatgpt (currently on free trial) as an assistant that keeps records of discussions, and keeping me on track. it provides me the prompts that i send to Grok and have created myself a simple Browser prototype game and its been generally successful but its not exactly state of the art. 

I'm also asking it to create a separate prompt for Claude but that's taking forever due to being on the free model but its definitely a much better result than Grok.

I'm wondering if i am taking full advantage of ChatGPT. its been very helpful but currently i dont even use Codex as i dont know how its any different from just the normal chat. I've been using the regular chat system and have multiple ones for different topics for the same game. 

  
if anyone has any tips and tricks, please do let me know so i can have better workflow. thank you all!

comments.author: shitty_advice_BDD
comments.body: Codex or Claude Code is what you really should use.

comments.author: radgh
comments.body: Codex is agentic which is different than chatgpt that just responds to you. It can do anything with your PC. You can ask it to build a game and it will write the code, generate models, etc. That would really boost your productivity but I'm not sure how well it works on a free tier. I prefer Claude code over codex but they are very similar.

comments.author: unfamily_friendly
comments.body:
Use codex or any other AI agent (Cursor IDE, Cherry Studio etc). It's a massive upgrade in all aspects.  
1) ask mode can see all your project files and answer based on the code. You can ask "where is the feature X implemented" and it will explain. It can even read the engine docs and source code. Really good for studying and debugging.  
2) Agent mode can do all above, plus writing code, plus running a game, plus watch screenshots and logs. It can kinda debug your game and repeat the fixes until it fully fixed. Imagine it like chat GPT can prompt itself

comments.author: Seerix
comments.body:
I have a claude and codex sub. I tell claude to have astra high do modeling in blender while claude implements the code. Codex also handles texture generation when needed. 

Works great.

comments.body: Why do you need one llm to make a prompt for another, are they having an affair?
